---
title: "Presets"
---

The preset menu at the top of the window has three sections:

- **Factory**: 21 presets meant for playing, with the dry signal on and the echo under it.
- **Examples**: the [listening examples](../listening.qmd), mostly *echo only* (dry off) so you hear just
  what memory returns.
- **User**: presets you've saved.

Every preset is listed with its settings in the [preset reference](../reference/presets.qmd).

## Loading

Choosing a preset sets the parameters it mentions and returns **everything else to its default**, so a preset
always sounds the same whatever you were doing before. Session settings are left alone: **Memory Budget**,
**Save Memory With Set** and the MIDI settings. Loading a preset never touches memory itself.

**<** and **>** step through the list.

## Saving your own

Click **Save…**, give the preset a name and, if you like, a description. It is saved as a text file in
`~/Music/MINERVA Space Echo/Presets/<name>.txt` and appears under **User**. To remove one, delete the file.

## The preset format

Presets are plain text, one `key = value` per line, using the parameter IDs from the
[parameter reference](../reference/parameters.qmd). Comment lines at the top are the description. Only settings
that differ from the defaults need to be listed:

```ini
# Self-match off and a sharp activation power: the bar you just played can't
# answer itself, so memory replies with the closest earlier bar.
capacity = 100
power = 9
self_match = off
echo_level_db = -4
```

Choices can be given by name (`sync_mode = Free`, `trace_division = 2 bars`) or index; on/off settings accept
`on`, `off`, `true`, `false`, `1`, `0`.

The offline renderer `mse-render` reads the same files, so a preset sounds the same offline as in Live. It also
understands **timed lines**, which change a setting at a given bar (counted from 0, in 4/4):

```ini
@8 freeze = on
@8.25 trace_division = 1/2
@2 command = clamp_all
```

The plug-in ignores timed lines. See [Offline tools](../reference/offline-tools.qmd).

::: {.callout-tip}
Live's own device presets (`.adv` files, saved from the device's title bar) work as well and store the
plug-in's full state, including memory if **Save Memory With Set** is on.
:::
